ONE BACKEND BUG FOUND (see backend_issues.critical) — /api/shop/businesses/{id}/menu happy_hour flag always returns false due to Mongo projection stripping happy_hour field before effective_points() is called.

critical.issue: The Mongo projection at routes/shop.py:150 (`{public_name:1, cover_urls:1, bigpoints:1}`) STRIPS the `happy_hour` field before passing profile to effective_points(). Result: response.happy_hour is ALWAYS false and response.points_multiplier is ALWAYS 1, even when merchant has enabled Happy Hour. Verified: PATCH /happy-hour with enabled=true, multiplier=2.0 → GET /happy-hour returns active_now=true, but GET /businesses/{bid}/menu still returns happy_hour=false + points_multiplier=1. Fix: add `happy_hour:1` to the projection (or drop projection). This breaks the entire consumer-facing Happy Hour boost feature — points_to_award on new orders won't get the 2X multiplier applied either? NO — /orders/checkout re-fetches the FULL profile (routes/marketplace_orders.py:92) so orders DO get the multiplier — only the /menu response indicator is wrong. Still HIGH priority because the consumer UI relies on this flag to render the 'Happy Hour · 2X' banner.

minor.issue: When merchant tries picked_up→picked_up the endpoint correctly rejects with 400 invalid_transition (since 'picked_up' not in ADVANCE map). However, canceling a picked_up order is still allowed (`new_status == 'canceled': pass`). Consider guarding 'canceled from picked_up' to prevent silent reversal after points were awarded — currently a merchant CAN cancel a picked_up order, and BigPoints already awarded stay awarded (no reversal). Data-integrity risk.

Pickup code is random 0000-9999. Not globally unique per business per day — two orders at the same merchant can collide on the same code, and the merchant would have no way to disambiguate. Consider making pickup_code unique per (business_id, active-order) or add order suffix.

action_items: (HIGH) Fix /app/backend/routes/shop.py:150 — remove or expand the projection on business_menu() so `happy_hour` is included in the profile doc passed to effective_points(). Suggested change: drop the projection entirely (this endpoint is fast on a single doc). This makes the consumer menu correctly reflect Happy Hour state on both mobile and web.

(MEDIUM) Persist RadioLife design variant to localStorage/cookie the moment user clicks 'Enable RadioLife' so Phase B web screens (/shop/menu/:id, /shop/orders, /shop/merchant/*) work on direct navigation, matching the mobile UX (carried over from iter56).

(MEDIUM) Enforce ordering on `picked_up` — do not allow cancel of an order that already reached picked_up, otherwise merchants can silently reverse a fulfilled order while BigPoints remain awarded (currently /marketplace_orders.py:260 allows cancel from ANY pre-pickup state, and this includes picked_up because the `elif ADVANCE.get(...) != new_status` branch is skipped for cancel).
(LOW) Make pickup_code unique per active order on the merchant (currently random 0000-9999 with per-order collisions possible).
(LOW) /api/merchant/marketplace/menu (list_menu) sorts by 'sort' which is set to base+i on bulk insert but doesn't compact after deletes. After many deletes, sort values are sparse — cosmetic only.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/shop.py:149-178 business_menu() — projection bug documented above. Also, this endpoint issues an unbounded find() over menu_items with no page limit. If a merchant loads 500+ items, all come back in one payload. Add a limit(200) OR paginate.

routes/marketplace_orders.py:262 update_order_status — the 'canceled from any pre-pickup state' branch is `pass` which allows canceling AFTER picked_up too (picked_up→canceled is NOT caught because the elif is short-circuited). Add explicit check `if o.status == 'picked_up' and new_status == 'canceled': reject`.

routes/marketplace_orders.py:87 checkout — the gift-card is auto-applied inside the checkout call itself, but the actual DB deduction happens only on payment success (via _finalize_paid). If the user creates a Stripe session and abandons it, the gift-card is 'reserved' in the order.gift_card_applied_cents but NOT deducted from gift_cards.balance_cents. Subsequent orders will use the SAME balance again — so the same gift-card credit can be reserved on multiple simultaneous orders. Consider soft-reserving with a pending_reservation on the gift_cards doc, or applying the deduction on order creation and refunding on cancel.

routes/marketplace_orders.py:212 order_status — polls Stripe on every consumer status GET when payment_status!='paid'. No rate limiting — a client refreshing the status view will hammer stripe.Session.retrieve. Add a 5s in-memory throttle keyed by session_id.

routes/marketplace_subscription.py:113 subscription_status — same unthrottled Stripe polling; also silently swallows exceptions on Stripe failure and returns pending — merchant can never see a real error.

routes/marketplace_menu.py:120 import_ai — catches ALL exceptions as 502 ai_import_failed with detail[:200]. This masks Pydantic validation errors from the LLM output (e.g. malformed items). Add structured logging with the raw LLM output for debug.
routes/marketplace_admin.py:191 comp_subscription — no admin_audit_log write; comping a business bypasses payment and should be traceable per PCI/marketplace compliance.

rca of the issue: BUG — /api/shop/businesses/{id}/menu returns happy_hour=false even when merchant enabled Happy Hour. REPRO: (1) merchant PATCHes /api/merchant/marketplace/happy-hour {enabled:true, start_hour:0, end_hour:23, multiplier:2.0}; (2) GET /api/merchant/marketplace/happy-hour returns active_now=true ✓; (3) GET /api/shop/businesses/{business_id}/menu returns happy_hour=false ✗. ROOT CAUSE: routes/shop.py:150 fetches the marketplace_profile with a projection {public_name:1, cover_urls:1, bigpoints:1} — the `happy_hour` field is EXCLUDED from the returned doc. Then effective_points(p) reads p.get('happy_hour') → gets None/empty → happy_hour_active() returns False. FIX: either drop the projection (single doc find is cheap) OR add `happy_hour:1` to it. Order-time points_to_award is unaffected because /orders/checkout re-fetches the full profile without projection, but the CONSUMER UI banner ('Happy Hour · 2X BigPoints') that reads /menu will never show up. All 27 other Phase B backend tests pass end-to-end.
